sweep_summary: huay1241 (Huaylla Wanca Quechua) is not in the catalog. All three title-keyword hits are 'categorical' noise (German focus prosody, Porteño Spanish nuclear accents, English word stress) — irrelevant, priority none. New in this search of works with stress in the title: an open archive.org scan of Cerrón-Palomino 1987 Lingüística quechua (saved), whose pp. 124/128 state penultimate stress as the general rule with final stress on the long-vowel 1st-person marker in Junín/Huanca forms (wasí-:, pulí-:); this refines the explicit variety-specific statement already held by the project from Ramírez Herrera 2014 (PUCP, p. 37: fixed predictable penultimate stress, citing Cerrón-Palomino 1967:58). Still unobtained and high priority: Cerrón-Palomino 1976 Gramática quechua: Junín-Huanca (HathiTrust search-only; Harvard print) and Cerrón-Palomino 1967 Fonología del wanka; medium: Cerrón-Palomino 1977 UIUC dissertation, Ráez 1917. web search and Google Books quotas were exhausted; sil.org, HathiTrust and IDEALS returned not reachable by automated download.

new_statements.quote: El acento en quechua huanca recae métricamente en la penúltima sílaba, razón por la cual es predecible y no genera oposiciones funcionales dentro de la lengua, como sí sucede en el castellano. Esta situación es aplicable a los préstamos también (Cerrón-Palomino 1967: 58). El carácter sistemático es claro y evidente en ejemplos como el siguiente: ['wa.si] 'casa' [wa.'si-lla] 'casita'. Como podemos ver, existe un esquema acentual fijo que recae siempre en la segunda sílaba de la palabra, contando de derecha a izquierda.
new_statements.translation: Stress in Huanca Quechua falls metrically on the penultimate syllable, for which reason it is predictable and does not create functional oppositions within the language, as it does in Spanish. This applies to loanwords as well (Cerrón-Palomino 1967: 58). The systematic character is clear and evident in examples like the following: ['wa.si] 'house', [wa.'si-lla] 'little house'. As we can see, there is a fixed stress pattern that always falls on the second syllable of the word counting from right to left.
new_statements.citation: Ramírez Herrera, Víctor Gonzalo. 2014. Vocales largas en los préstamos del castellano al quechua huanca: un acercamiento descriptivo y explicativo del fenómeno. Tesis de Licenciado en Lingüística, PUCP, Lima (advisor R. Cerrón-Palomino).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word (second syllable from the right), regardless of suffixation (wasi -> wa'si-lla); it is predictable and non-contrastive, and holds for Spanish loans too.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for native words. Spanish proparoxytone loans are re-stressed on the penult, the former stressed vowel surviving as length ([a.'ni.mu] < ánimo, [sa.'ba.du] < sábado). Vowel length is phonemic but the thesis does not describe any interaction of length with stress placement.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, including suffixed forms; data from elicited word lists (citation forms) and recordings with 10 speakers of waylla huanca in Huancán, Huayucachi, Viques and Huacrapuquio (Huancayo province). The rule is attributed to Cerrón-Palomino 1967: 58.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source explicitly restricts itself to 'waylla huanca' (provinces of Huancayo and Chupaca), i.e. huay1241 itself, with data collected in the districts of Huancán, Huayucachi, Viques and Huacrapuquio on the periphery of Huancayo; it distinguishes this from waycha (Concepción) and shawsha (Jauja) huanca. The Wroughton 1996 fragment held by the project is Shausha (Jauja) Huanca, ISO qxw, a sister language-level variety, not huay1241.

new_statements.quote: Es de advertirse que en las formas del juninense el acento recae en la última sílaba ([wasí-:], [pulí-:], etc.), al par que en las del ayacuchano, aquél se coloca, como es de uso en el quechua sureño, en la penúltima sílaba ([wási-y], [purí-ni], etc.). (p. 124) [...] hecho inusitado en el resto de las variedades en donde prima la acentuación penúltima. [...] como lo fue la acentuación aguda (aparte del acento enfático) que acompaña a la marca de la persona posesora-actora en los dialectos centroperuanos (p. 128)
new_statements.translation: Note that in the Junín forms the stress falls on the final syllable ([wasí-:] 'my house', [pulí-:] 'I walk', etc.), whereas in the Ayacucho forms it is placed, as is usual in Southern Quechua, on the penultimate syllable ([wási-y], [purí-ni], etc.). [...] an unusual fact in the rest of the varieties, where penultimate stress prevails. [...] as was the final (oxytone) stress (apart from emphatic stress) that accompanies the possessor/actor person marker in the central Peruvian dialects.
new_statements.citation: Cerrón-Palomino, Rodolfo (1987). Lingüística quechua. Cuzco: Centro de Estudios Rurales Andinos 'Bartolomé de Las Casas'. §4.34 p. 124 and §4.5 'Fonología suprasegmental' p. 128.
new_statements.reading: First-hand, from the Wanka native-speaker grammarian (scanned errors 'reeae'/'3a' normalized to 'recae'/'la'). Default word stress in Huanca (Junín) Quechua is penultimate; a word-final long vowel (the 1st-person possessor/actor marker -:) carries the stress, giving final stress in forms like wasí-: and pulí-: (pulí- with /l/ < *r is specifically Huanca). Corroborated and made variety-specific by Ramírez Herrera 2014 (PUCP thesis on Waylla huanca of Huancayo, p. 37): 'El acento en quechua huanca recae métricamente en la penúltima sílaba.. predecible y no genera oposiciones funcionales.. aplicable a los préstamos también (Cerrón-Palomino 1967: 58)'. Suggested coding: penultimate, fixed and predictable, with final long vowels stressed (quantity-sensitive at the right edge). The canonical statement would be Cerrón-Palomino 1967 'Fonología del wanka' p. 58 or the 1976 Gramática quechua: Junín-Huanca, neither obtainable open.

II §2.2 (pp. 37-38): stress falls metrically on the penultimate syllable, predictable, non-contrastive, applies to loans too (citing Cerrón-Palomino 1967: 58); wasi / wa'si-lla; Spanish proparoxytones shift stress to the penult leaving length on the old stressed vowel (a:'nimu < ánimo). Restated in conclusions p. 40. Data: waylla huanca, districts Huancán, Huayucachi, Viques, Huacrapuquio (Huancayo).

sources.quote: Es de advertirse que en las formas del juninense el acento recae en la última sílaba ([wasí-:], [pulí-:], etc.), al par que en las del ayacuchano, aquél se coloca, como es de uso en el quechua sureño, en la penúltima sílaba ([wási-y], [purí-ni], etc.). (p. 124) ... hecho inusitado en el resto de las variedades en donde prima la acentuación penúltima. ... como lo fue la acentuación aguda (aparte del acento enfático) que acompaña a la marca de la persona posesora-actora en los dialectos centroperuanos (p. 128)
sources.note: By the Huanca-speaking Wanka specialist. Penultimate stress is the general rule ('prima la acentuación penúltima'); in the Junín/Huanca dialect (examples wasí-: 'my house', pulí-: 'I walk' — pulí- with /l/ is the Huanca form) stress falls on the final syllable when it carries the long-vowel 1st-person marker; i.e. penultimate with final long vowels attracting stress. Statement is at dialect-group level (juninense / centroperuano) with Huanca examples. Also notes (p. 128) that suprasegmentals are the least understood part of Quechua phonology. Language not in catalog, so no coding to confirm.
